explanation.question_quote: A 27-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 3-day history of a sore throat and fever. Her temperature is 38.5°C (101.3°F). Examination shows edematous oropharyngeal mucosa and enlarged tonsils with purulent exudate. There is tender cervical lymphadenopathy.
explanation.sentence: She has an acute febrile sore throat with purulent tonsillar exudate and tender cervical lymphadenopathy.
This pattern is characteristic of group A streptococcal pharyngitis.
Toxic shock syndrome is the best listed option because it can complicate severe invasive group A streptococcal infection, although it is rare after uncomplicated pharyngitis.
Acute rheumatic fever is a classic sequela of untreated streptococcal pharyngitis, but its characteristic cardiac manifestation is valvulitis, not dilated cardiomyopathy.
